title: Materials Update: Pbr Map & Texture Editor | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
This new update to Materials in CLO 2025.0 allows you to choose the file format when saving an image and merge multiple layers into a single file. When applying a texture, other PBR maps are automatically loaded according to the naming convention. 
Check out other new features here: https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord?utm_campaign=multi_item_banner_JointheOfficialCLODiscord&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=later-linkinbio

summary: ```markdown # Materials Update: PBR Map & Texture Editor | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, my name is Phoebe, and I have some great updates to share with you regarding materials, especially with our Multi-Texture Editor and PBR maps. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn! ## Changing Fabric and Base Maps Here I have my garment, but I want a different fabric. What I'm going to do is select my fabric and change out my base maps. I have all the maps ready, and now, with this update, I can add them all in at once—super cool! ### Adding Texture Maps So, I’m going to open this up and select the map I want. As you can see, I’ve made sure to name all of these properly. I have ABC base, displacement, metal, normal, opacity, and rough. They are all named correctly. You can choose to use short names or the full names, like normal, displacement, metal, opacity, and roughness. Once I hit open, a pop-up appears asking, "After adding the texture image, the other PBR maps of this material will automatically update. Would you like to proceed?" I’m going to say yes, and now you’ll see all of the maps show up here. Isn’t that cool? ## Using the Multi-Texture Editor Now, this is a really nice colorway, but maybe I want to add a print or something different. So, I’m going to go into the handy-dandy Multi-Texture Editor. I will open the texture editor and add in some other artwork that I know I want to include. ### Resizing and Creating Prints I’m going to hit add and resize this new texture. Looks cool! Now I’ll add another one—this one is nice. I’m just creating a little fun print here. Once I’m happy with my design, this is the cool update: I can go to the next page and click on it to save everything out. ## Saving Options I can save these all individually or merge them together. I’m going to choose "Save Merge Layer Together." I can also select which ones I want to save and which ones I don’t. Using these checkboxes, I can uncheck the ones I don't want to save. Since I already have the base map, I’m going to uncheck this option. I can also choose the file format: PNG, JPEG, or TIFF. I’m going to go with PNG because I already have a lot of empty backgrounds, and I don’t want to edit those. ### Finalizing the Save I’ll save the merged layer as a PNG and hit okay. Now, I’m going to select the folder, and I’ve had all of them saved right here. Here they are, all merged together—pretty cool, right? I can now hit apply and close, and now I’ve got my new print and my new fabric. ## Conclusion I hope you enjoyed the video and are excited to try all of this out. If you have any questions, use the comment section down below. Don't forget to like and subscribe and check out our Clo channel—there are so many things to learn. Thanks again, and keep having fun. Have a great day! ```
